title: chard measurement report
description: One report is one environment, toolchain and profile measured by the full probe set, an append-only fact that comparison tables join on the column key (environment.distro.id, environment.distro.version_id, toolchain.id, profile.id) and the row key observations[].check, of which observations[].flag is only the display spelling. A check id that changes is a new row: no alias map exists.

chard_schema.description: The major version of this document's shape, which moves under the CLI contract's rule (`chard --help`; DESIGN.md, "The command-line contract"): an added key is no change, so every object admits one, except the predicate definitions under `$defs`, which stay closed so an evaluator refuses a key it does not know. `1` at chard's first publication; `2` since `decoders.language` names `chard-predicate/2`.

id.description: Sixteen hex digits of a SHA-256 over `inputs=<run.inputs_sha256>` and each observation's check, verdict and level, sorted, one `cell=` line each, so two identical measurements share an id and the clock is no input. The `run-id-disagrees-with-measurement` consistency rule recomputes it.

inputs_sha256.description: Sixty-four lowercase hex digits: the SHA-256 over canonical `key=value` lines of what the run was asked to measure (the schema version, the harness, corpus, deadlines, check selection and structured-diagnostics request, the profile, the toolchain and its linkers, and the distribution, C library, kernel, CPU, execution mode and image attestation), so two runs asked the same thing share it whatever they found. The clock, the invocation, prose, derived fields, evidence_filters and every result are left out, and the `run-id-disagrees-with-measurement` consistency rule recomputes it.

duration_ms.x-volatile: Wall-clock time of the whole run. 0 under --normalize.

harness_revision.description: VCS revision of the harness, if known.

harness_revision_source.description: Which source named run.harness_revision: the tree the harness was compiled from (`git`, a `git archive`'s `REVISION` file as `archive`, a crate's `.cargo_vcs_info.json` as `cargo-vcs`), or `CHARD_REVISION` at build time as `asserted`, which nothing checks, so an asserted revision joins only reports asserted alike. Absent exactly where run.harness_revision is.

harness_rustflags_sha256.description: Sixty-four lowercase hex digits: the SHA-256 of the rustflags cargo built the harness under (`CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`), so a report carrying one joins only reports built under the same flags. Absent where cargo passed none.

probe_corpus_sha256.description: Sixty-four lowercase hex digits: the SHA-256 over every field of every probe and check in the corpus but prose and cross-references, and over run.decoders_sha256, so two reports carrying one value were measured by one corpus read by one set of decoders. `table` and `matrix` refuse to mix values.

decoders_sha256.description: Sixty-four lowercase hex digits, as `chard probes` publishes it: the SHA-256 over the predicate language version, every check's predicate in canonical form, and the source of every file that decides what a report says about a check, comments and test modules stripped. Folded into run.probe_corpus_sha256 and published on its own, so a reader whose two reports' corpus hashes differ can tell whether the code did.

invocation.description: The harness's argv, argv[0] reduced to the text after its last `/` and each invalid UTF-8 sequence replaced by U+FFFD, so the values of --workdir, --output, -o and --image-attestation are the paths the operator wrote. Under --normalize argv[0] reads `chard` and those values read `<normalized>`; every other argument stays.
invocation.x-volatile: Names where this run put things. Path-valued options are replaced under --normalize.

deadlines.description: Every deadline that could have shaped a value in this report, in whole milliseconds: a probe run still going at `probe_run_ms` is killed and reads `timed_out`, a compile still going at `compile_ms` is killed and recorded as failed, and `compile_drain_grace_ms` bounds reading a compiler's output after it exits.

probe_run_ms.description: `--timeout`, applied to each probe run on its own. Every run record's `deadline_ms` carries the same value.

artifact_witness.description: The nonce this run placed in a `.note.chard.run` section of every translation unit compiled to code, and held each ELF artifact to before reading it: one carrying another value or none is not read or run, and every check over it is `indeterminate` under `artifact-lacks-run-witness`, so an object a compiler cache or wrapper served from an earlier run is withheld. It is no input to run.inputs_sha256 or run.id and is absent on a macOS run, whose Mach-O artifacts the ELF reader does not read; THREAT_MODEL.md lists what it does not hold, a macro dump and a compile forwarded to another compiler among them.

source.description: `os-random`: 128 bits from the operating system for this run alone, so no artifact of another run carries the nonce. `derived`, under `--normalize`: the first 128 bits of a SHA-256 over the flag lists, the `--env` pairs, the driver, its version line and target triple, and run.probe_corpus_sha256, so two runs of one measurement publish the same artifact digests, and an object a cache kept from an earlier run of the same question carries it and is read.

nonce.description: Thirty-two lowercase hex digits, the value every stored `elf` entry's `run_witness` holds. Under `os-random` it and every artifact digest (`build.artifact_sha256`, the keys of `facts`) differ between two runs of one measurement; it carries no `x-volatile` mark because --normalize zeroes nothing here and asks for a `derived` nonce instead.

environment.description: Where the measurement happened. Distinct from `toolchain`: the same toolchain measured under a different kernel can give different runtime verdicts.

id.description: os-release ID, e.g. ubuntu, fedora, alpine, arch, debian.

arch.description: The architecture chard's own binary was compiled for, e.g. x86_64, aarch64, which is the kernel's only while chard runs natively: under qemu-user an aarch64 chard on an x86_64 kernel publishes `aarch64` here. `machine` is the kernel's own word.

machine.description: The kernel's own machine, from Linux's `/proc/sys/kernel/arch`, which qemu-user does not intercept, compared with each runtime artifact's `elf.machine` to decide `run-under-emulation`. Absent where the file is absent (every non-Linux platform, and Linux kernels older than the sysctl).

is_host_kernel.description: True when environment.execution.mode is container, where the kernel is the host's rather than the measured distro's. Derived from the mode alone, so it is false on a host by default as on an asserted host or vm, and `ownership` says which.

ownership.description: Whose kernel the run's is, from the mode read with mode_evidence.basis, which decides the checks that declare needs_vm: `own` where the operator asserted `host` or `vm`, which nothing chard reads corroborates, and they are measured; `borrowed` where the mode is `container`, and they are withheld under `needs-vm`; `unsettled` on the default `assumed-host` basis, and they are withheld under `execution-mode-assumed`. Held to the mode and basis by `kernel-ownership-disagrees-with-execution-mode`; `table` and `matrix` still read a report without it, held on `is_host_kernel` alone, and `matrix` names its cell `unpublished`.

impl.description: The C library chard detected; the enumeration is every name chard can write.

relevant_features.description: The features that gate a hardening mechanism (ibt, shstk, user_shstk, smap, smep, bti, paca, pacg, gcs), spelt as /proc/cpuinfo spells them, since a binary can be marked for one on a CPU that cannot enforce it. Empty where the host advertises none of them, and where it has no /proc/cpuinfo (OpenBSD, macOS).

arm_parts.description: The distinct `CPU implementer:CPU part` pairs aarch64 /proc/cpuinfo lists, as the kernel spells them (`0x41:0xd0c`, Arm Neoverse N1), in the order the cores first show them: the record of which CPU the run had, since that file names no vendor or model there. Absent where none is listed: on x86, and without /proc/cpuinfo.

mode.description: container shares the host kernel; kernel-enforced runtime probes are only valid under vm or host.

detection.description: How the execution mode was determined, recorded so a reader can judge how much to trust it.

image_attestation.description: What established that the system measured is the image this report names, present even where nothing did so that no omission reads as nothing to report. chard runs inside the image and cannot verify it, so an attestation is recorded as received, not as a verification chard performed.

status.description: not-applicable when measuring the running system; unattested when an image was named with nothing carried in to support the name; attested when a fetcher's provenance object was supplied. A digest mismatch never appears here: measure refuses to publish.

established_by.description: What the reader is being asked to trust, in words.

verdict.description: The fetcher's own verdict: signature-verified, signed-unpinned, digest-matched, unverified. A digest matching a manifest served over TLS is weaker than a digest under a signature.

served_by.description: Host that served the bytes; a mirror where the publisher uses a redirector.

origin.description: How `url` came to be known, strongest first: `recorded-at-fetch`, the fetcher wrote it as it downloaded; `confirmed-by-refetch`, the publisher was shown to serve identical bytes there, not that this copy came from there; `not-recorded`, the chain stops at a local file. Absent, it reads as `not-recorded`.

manifest_fetched.description: Whether the publisher's manifest was retrieved at all: a manifest that disagrees with the image is refused, while no manifest to compare against says nothing about the bytes and yields `unattested`. Absent, it reads as true.

installed_disk.description: The disk that booted, present only where it is not the artifact `digest` names but one installed from it (absent, never null, otherwise), received from the fetcher's install record, since chard runs on that disk and cannot hash it. Hashed into run.inputs_sha256, so two installed disks give two input digests.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the installed disk image, recorded after the install and re-checked by the fetcher before every boot.

installed_at.description: When the installer started, UTC. For a rolling branch such as Alpine edge this dates every package installed.

installed_from_digest.description: The digest, in `digest_kind`, of the artifact installed from. chard refuses an attestation in which this differs from `digest`.

mode_evidence.description: What chard observed about the execution mode, beside what it was told, present always so that `host` by default reads apart from `host` by assertion. chard's own instruments settle `container` or nothing, never `host`.

basis.description: asserted-and-contradicted never appears: the consistency pass refuses such a report, since it is two claims about one property that disagree.

observed.description: What chard observed. Absent when no instrument settled it, which is not the same as host.

observation.description: The instrument that settled `container` (a runtime's marker file, a cgroup needle, systemd's `/run/systemd/container`, a `container=` word on PID 1, or a user namespace) and what it returned. Where none did, what each of the two positive markers read: absent, unreadable (which claims nothing about presence), empty, or without the word.

id.description: The join key across reports, `kind-version-libc-distro`, as in "gcc-16.1.1-glibc2.43-fedora44". The libc tag is `environment.libc.impl` and `version` run together (the implementation alone where no version was read), and the distribution tag `environment.distro.id` and `version_id` (the id alone where the version is `unknown`).

version_raw.description: The first line of the driver's `--version`, verbatim: empty where it printed nothing, and absent, with a warning diagnostic under `toolchain.version_raw`, where it did not exit 0 with its output whole. `kind` and `version` come from the macro dump, and an error diagnostic under the same context names a banner of another compiler family.

driver.description: Path to the compiler driver actually invoked.

driver_resolved.description: `driver` with every symbolic link followed, such as the cache behind a compiler cache's masquerade entry; a wrapper that is a file of its own resolves to itself. Evidence only: chard decides nothing by it, `run.inputs_sha256` digests `driver`, and it is absent where the path did not resolve.

configure_args.description: `gcc -v`'s `Configured with:` line, where `--enable-default-pie` and `--enable-default-ssp` show: the provenance of the `bare` defaults.

config_files.description: The configuration files the driver announced loading in `-v` (clang's `Configuration file:`, gcc's `Reading specs from`), a distribution-defaults mechanism `--version` does not show. Where the list is non-empty, a `bare` column's `profile.flags_source` reads `driver-config-file`.

linker.description: The linker the profile links with, and what the linked artifacts said about that identity; the object is `$defs/linker`.

target.description: The architecture every arch gate was decided under, before any build, held to four witnesses: the `e_machine` of the run's ELF artifacts, and the architecture macros of the driver's dump with no flags (`macros`), under the profile's C flags (`profile_macros`) and through the C++ driver under its C++ flags (`profile_macros_cxx`). A witness under which a check's gate decides otherwise withholds that check `indeterminate` under `gating.rule: target-arch-contradicted`, and a machine, width or byte order the mechanism table has no row for (`abi`) withholds every arch-gated check.

arch.description: The value compared against each check's architecture list: `x86_64`, `x86`, `aarch64`, or the first component of `target_triple` as the driver printed it.

source.description: `dumpmachine`: the first component of the driver's `-dumpmachine` answer (`target_triple`); `kernel`: `environment.kernel.arch`, where `-dumpmachine` gave nothing to parse; `profile-macros`: the one architecture macro `profile_macros` defined, where the profile's C flags select a target, which the flagless `-dumpmachine` cannot see, and that dump completed.

agreement.description: `agrees`: every ELF artifact read carries `arch`'s machine family; `disagrees`: one carries another family, or the artifacts carry more than one, with an error diagnostic under `toolchain.target`; `unmapped`: `arch` names no family chard maps and the artifacts carry one; `no-elf-artifact`: nothing was read (a Mach-O host, or a selection that builds nothing), so `arch` stands uncorroborated.

machines.description: The stored `elf.machine` of the observations' builds to the number of distinct artifacts, by `build.artifact_sha256`, that carry it.

artifacts_read.description: Distinct ELF artifacts read, relocatables included: the compiler's `e_machine` is in a `.o` as in a linked output.

evidence.description: The machines, the first artifact carrying each, where `arch` came from, and why the agreement follows.

abi.description: The width and byte order of the read family's artifacts, and of each dump that agreed about the family, held to the ones the mechanism table's rows for `arch` stand for.

expected.description: The width and order `arch`'s rows stand for, the hosts they were measured on; absent where `arch` has no row in the table.

artifacts.description: Each `ELF<class> <order>` among the artifacts of the read family, to the number of distinct artifacts, by `build.artifact_sha256`, carrying it. A record with no `elf_data` is left out.

dumps.description: Each dump whose agreement about the family is `agrees` and that defined `__SIZEOF_POINTER__` and `__BYTE_ORDER__`, by the name the evidence gives it, to the `ELF<class> <order>` those two name.

agreement.description: `agrees`: every artifact and dump read carries `expected`; `disagrees`: one carries another width or order, which withholds every arch-gated check under `target-abi-contradicted`; `unmapped`: `arch` has no row, so nothing is expected; `no-witness`: nothing read named a width and order.

evidence.description: What `arch`'s rows stand for, what each witness carried, and why the agreement follows.

macros.description: The second witness: the architecture macros of the driver's intrinsic dump (`cc -dM -E`) with no profile flags, as `-dumpmachine` is asked, which exists on a run that reads no ELF artifact. It names the driver's own target; a target the profile's flags select is `profile_macros`'s to witness.

defined.description: The architecture macros the dump defined, in the order listed: `__x86_64__` (machine `x86_64`), `__i386__` (`i386`) and `__aarch64__` (`aarch64`). Held to `predefined_macros` where that is published, and only to define none outside these where its dump errored or is empty.

agreement.description: `agrees`: the dump defines the macro of `arch`'s family and no other; `disagrees`: another family's macro, more than one, or none under an `arch` of the three families, which withholds each arch-gated check whose gate decides otherwise under the machine it witnesses, and is published with an error diagnostic under `toolchain.target`; `overruled`: none of the three under such an `arch`, while every ELF artifact carries its family and one was built by a probe of the dump's language, so the dump withholds nothing; `unmapped`: `arch` names no family chard maps and the dump defines one macro; `no-arch-macro`: none of the three under an `arch` of none of their families; `superseded`: `source` is `profile-macros`, so this flagless dump names the driver's default target and withholds nothing.

evidence.description: The macros, the machine each names, where `arch` came from, and why the agreement follows.

abi.description: The `ELF<class> <order>` the dump's `__SIZEOF_POINTER__` (4 or 8) and `__BYTE_ORDER__` name, absent where it did not define both. Published whatever the agreement; `abi` reads it only under `agrees`.

profile_macros.description: The third witness, present exactly where `profile.cflags` and `profile.ldflags` are not both empty: the same dump under those flags, which witnesses a target they select on a run that reads no ELF artifact. It witnesses every C probe, and every C++ probe where `profile_macros_cxx` is absent.

flags.description: The flags the dump ran under, before `-dM -E`: `profile.cflags` then `profile.ldflags`, the list a C probe's measured variant is built with.

stdout_unterminated.description: Present, and true, where the dump's output was cut off partway through a line (`build_record.stdout_unterminated`), whatever its exit status; its agreement is then `dump-failed`. Absent otherwise.

macros_defined.description: Every macro the dump defined, counted.

defined.description: The architecture macros this dump defined, in the order `macros.defined` lists them. Empty under `dump-failed`.

agreement.description: As `macros.agreement`, plus `dump-failed`: the dump exited non-zero, defined no macro (a flag the driver refused) or was cut off (`stdout_unterminated`), so it witnesses nothing and `defined` is empty.

evidence.description: The macros, the machine each names, where `arch` came from, the flags, and why the agreement follows.

abi.description: As `macros.abi`: the `ELF<class> <order>` this dump's `__SIZEOF_POINTER__` and `__BYTE_ORDER__` name, where it defined both; absent where it defined one or neither.

profile_macros_cxx.description: The fourth witness: the same dump through the C++ driver under the list a C++ probe's measured variant is built with (`profile.cxxflags`, or `profile.cflags` where that is empty, then `profile.ldflags`), present exactly where `toolchain.cxx_driver` is and that list differs from `profile_macros`'s. It witnesses the C++ probes in place of `profile_macros`, and is taken whatever the probe selection, so on a selection with no C++ probe a `disagrees` withholds nothing.

flags.description: The flags the dump ran under, before `-dM -E`: the list a C++ probe's measured variant is built with.

stdout_unterminated.description: Present, and true, where the dump's output was cut off partway through a line (`build_record.stdout_unterminated`), whatever its exit status; its agreement is then `dump-failed`. Absent otherwise.

macros_defined.description: Every macro the dump defined, counted.

defined.description: The architecture macros this dump defined, in the order `macros.defined` lists them. Empty under `dump-failed`.

agreement.description: As `profile_macros.agreement`, for the macros this dump defined.

evidence.description: The macros, the machine each names, where `arch` came from, the flags, and why the agreement follows.

abi.description: As `macros.abi`: the `ELF<class> <order>` this dump's `__SIZEOF_POINTER__` and `__BYTE_ORDER__` name, where it defined both; absent where it defined one or neither.

predefined_macros_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the `cc -dM -E` dump taken with no flags and the C library's headers included, as sorted `name=value` lines. Two toolchains with equal hashes have identical macro-channel defaults.

predefined_macros.description: The dump `predefined_macros_sha256` is over, name -> value (empty string when defined with no value), present only under `--emit-macros`.

fhardened_fortify.description: The driver's intrinsic dump under `-fhardened -O2`, with no profile flag, and its control under `-O2` alone (`baseline`), taken on every run: where the dump answers what the option asks, `fhardened-effective`'s fortify slot takes its bar from `fortify_source`, and otherwise from `environment.libc` and `target_triple`, with the slot's `note` saying why. The dump answers where both exited 0 with their output whole and defined macros, no stderr line names `-fhardened` or `-Whardened` (`diagnostic`), and the control defines no `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` or a lower one; a profile flag that changes the level the option asks (`-specs=`, `-mmusl`, `--sysroot`) is outside this reading.

flags.description: The flags the dump ran under, before `-dM -E`: `-fhardened`, `-O2`.

stdout_unterminated.description: Present and true where the dump's output was cut off partway through a line.

diagnostic.description: The first line of the dump's stderr naming `-fhardened` or `-Whardened`, verbatim.

fortify_source.description: The value the dump defined `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` to, verbatim.

baseline.description: The control: the same dump under `-O2` alone, without `-fhardened`. A level it defines equal to `fortify_source` is not the option's own, and a control that did not exit 0 whole, or defined no macro, attributes nothing.

libc_headers_error.description: How the dump of the libc-identification headers failed, whether or not macros came out: `exited N` or `was killed by a signal`, then `: ` and its first non-empty stderr line where it wrote one, or `exited 0 with its output cut off partway through a line`; absent on a clean dump. Where present, `environment.libc.detection` names the failure, a library is identified only from a macro the dump printed, and `environment.libc.impl` is `unknown` where none names one.

profile.description: Which of the two-questions-never-to-conflate this report answers.

id.description: bare | bare-optimized | openssf-tldr | explicit:<digest>, a column join key: `explicit:` carries the first twelve hex digits of flags_sha256, so two flag lists are two columns, and a run given --env pairs adds `+env:` and twelve hex digits of a SHA-256 over the pairs, sorted by name, each NAME=VALUE, NUL-separated. `bare-optimized` is the compiler's defaults plus -O2 alone, which fortify needs to exist, and a distribution's own build flags are measured through `explicit`.

flags_sha256.description: A SHA-256 over `cflags`, `cxxflags` and `ldflags` in that order, each flag separated by U+001F and each list by a newline. Published on every profile, so two columns under one built-in id whose flags differ differ in a field a join can read.

flags_source.description: `none`: no flag was passed and the driver loaded no configuration file, so the report measures compiled-in defaults; `driver-config-file`: no flag was passed but the driver loaded one (toolchain.config_files), whose flags chard does not read and would otherwise credit to the compiler. `chard-enabling-condition`: chard passed a flag that grants no hardening but is needed to observe some (-O2 alone), so a reader does not credit it to the distribution, and toolchain_note names any configuration file behind it.

guide_revision.description: On the openssf-tldr profile only, and always there: the OpenSSF guide's revision, by the date in its by-line (YYYY-MM-DD), whose rows the profile's flags are built from, since the id stays the same when the rows change. It names the rows, not the flags, which also depend on the architecture, so profile.cflags stays the record of what was passed.

toolchain_note.description: How the query was made, and what was assumed if no selector was used.

compiler_environment.description: The complete environment every toolchain invocation of the run received (detection, macro dumps, listings and probe builds): the variables in passed and in set, and nothing else, so a toolchain configured through a variable such as a Nix cc-wrapper's NIX_HARDENING_ENABLE is measured as configured only where set holds it. A probe's own run is described by its run record's environment instead.

passed.description: Variables handed over from chard's own environment, by name: PATH where chard has one. The value is withheld because it names the operator's directories.

set.description: Variables set to a value, name to value: the pins every invocation receives (LC_ALL=C, TERM=dumb, CCACHE_DISABLE=1, CCACHE_CONFIGPATH=/dev/null) and the run's --env pairs, which profile.id's `+env:` digest covers. The pins are what chard hands the first program on PATH, so one in front of ccache that unsets them leaves them listed here (THREAT_MODEL.md, "A compiler cache on PATH").

observations.description: One entry per probe. The raw facts; `matrix` is derived from these.

facts.description: The artifacts and `-dM -E` dumps the observations and their control arms were read from, once per digest, keyed by `build.artifact_sha256` or a dump record's `stdout_sha256`; `fact-store-disagrees-with-references` refuses a report whose references and entries disagree in either direction, and `{}` means nothing was built. A reader meeting a `kind` outside `$defs/fact_entry`'s enumeration reads that entry as not understood, never as the absence of facts.

listings.description: The driver's answers the listing rules read, by probe id: the `-###` link and compile listings and the `-print-search-dirs` answers, parsed, each with the flags it was asked under, and what the comparisons read of the filesystem (`paths`); the raw text is not kept, since gcc's names temporary files anew on every run. `chard detect` replays each observation's listing rules over these answers, and takes a report without the member as written (`listings-unpublished`), except where its run.decoders_sha256 is the replaying binary's, whose code always publishes the member, so its absence disagrees.

decoders.description: The predicates the readings in `observations` were evaluated with, once per report: every check that publishes a `decoded` reading has an entry, and no other check does. Absent when no reading was published.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the predicate's canonical form, compact `serde_json`, the digest `chard probes` publishes for the check's decoder.

fortify_ratchet.description: The _FORTIFY_SOURCE rungs, derived as two axes the flag conflates: `whole_object_level`, how precisely an object is bounded, and `dynamic_bounds`, whether sizes unknown at compile time are bounded. Under glibc the rungs nest, so a non-monotone set means a probe is faulty: every derived field is withheld and the rungs' verdicts are downgraded.

implied_level.description: The point on glibc's ladder the two axes give: (0,no)->0, (1,no)->1, (2,no)->2, (2,yes)->3. Absent, never null, for any other pair, such as fortify-headers' dynamic bounds without subobject bounds; a consumer gating on a level then reads the axes.

whole_object_level.description: How precisely the implementation bounds an object: `0` none, `1` the whole object only (__builtin_object_size(p,0)), `2` a struct member apart from the object enclosing it. Absent when no rung was decided.

dynamic_bounds.description: Whether sizes unknown at compile time are bounded (__builtin_dynamic_object_size rather than __builtin_object_size), independent of `whole_object_level`. Absent when the rung was withheld.

implementation.description: The fortify implementation the rungs were measured against, as the probes' `.chard.report` section names it; absent when no probe named one. Only `glibc` nests the levels as the ratchet assumes: `fortify-headers` has no subobject bounds, so its dynamic rung fires with the subobject rung silent, and `apple` and `freebsd` (15 and later) clamp a request above 2 to 2, so their dynamic rung cannot fire.

structured_diagnostics.description: Present only under `--structured-diagnostics`: the gate's count of its own work against what was eligible, so a gate that compared nothing cannot read as agreement. Each disagreeing or undecodable arm is also a warning in `diagnostics`.

format.description: The side build's flag. Absent where no structured form is known for the toolchain, which a diagnostic also says.

checks_eligible.description: Observations of checks the structured decoder has needles for.

not_compared.description: Eligible checks with no comparison: withheld before their arms were built, or measured on a toolchain with no structured form. `checks_compared` plus this list's length is `checks_eligible`.

arms_expected.description: The arms the compared checks' comparisons were fed, summed: each comparison's `arms_expected`.

arms_missing.description: Of `arms_expected`, the arms with no build or no side build, which were not compared: `arms_compared` plus this is `arms_expected`. The consistency rule `structured-diagnostics-disagrees-with-observations` recomputes every count here.

corroboration.description: Protections measured through more than one channel, and whether the channels agree, so that a macro claiming a protection the artifact shows absent, as a spec file patching one compiler job and not the other produces, is visible rather than resolved in favour of one channel.

verdicts.description: Only members that produced a measurement. A withheld verdict can neither corroborate nor contradict.

measured_channels.description: How many distinct channels produced a measurement, which a withheld member's channel does not, so this and not channels.length is the number that can agree. A `partial` at a level that instruments only code marked to opt in (`ssp-level` at `explicit`) is listed under `verdicts` and counts toward no channel, since no probe opts in.

corroborated.description: True only when measured_channels >= 2. Distinct from `agree`: one measuring channel beside a withheld member does not disagree, but the protection rests on that one channel, as it does where the only macro-channel member reads `partial` at an opt-in level.

withheld.description: Members that produced no measurement, mapped to the verdict that withheld them. Listed rather than dropped, so a reader can see which channel is blind and why.

sources.description: What each measuring member read, keyed by check. A withheld member, which `withheld` names, and a member reading `partial` at an opt-in level, which `verdicts` lists, are absent: neither is a witness the others are checked against.

witness.description: `artifact` for a member that read the probe's output: its headers, its `.chard.report` self-report, or a run of it. `preprocessor-dump` for a macro read from `cc -dM -E` because no artifact carried a self-report. `compiler-stderr` for a diagnostic stream.

artifact_sha256.description: The artifact the member read, or the build whose stderr it read. Absent for a preprocessor dump and wherever the build recorded no artifact.

independent_witnesses.description: How many distinct witnesses the measuring members read: one per build, its stderr and artifact together, and one per preprocessor dump. Not measured_channels, since three channels over one probe's build read one artifact a fault in that build reaches alike, and not toolchains, since every witness is output of the same compiler and flag list.

composites.description: Umbrella options answered by reducing over the measured checks, kept apart from `observations` because a composite is arithmetic over measurements, not one. The reduction is three-valued: a constituent measured absent settles the umbrella whatever could not be measured, and an unmeasurable constituent prevents a positive verdict.

id.description: Stable identifier for the umbrella, e.g. `fhardened-effective`.

derived_from.description: Check ids this verdict was reduced from. Named so no reader mistakes the result for a measurement.

reason.description: Why this verdict, naming the constituents that decided it.

flag.description: The flag as the umbrella's own documentation names it.

check.description: The chard check consulted for this requirement: on `fhardened-effective`'s `-fstack-protector-strong` slot the graded `ssp-level-emitted`, since the presence-only `canary-emitted` cannot tell plain `-fstack-protector` from `-strong`.

applicable.description: False where the requirement does not apply here at all, such as `-fcf-protection` off x86. Inapplicable constituents drop out of the reduction rather than counting as shortfalls.

level.description: Measured level, where the requirement is about strength rather than presence: on `fhardened-effective`'s `-fstack-protector-strong` slot, `ssp-level-emitted`'s level (`explicit`, `basic`, `strong`, `all` or `unsafe-frame`) wherever that check published one.

satisfied.description: Deprecated, kept for one schema generation: true only when state is `in-force` or `marked`. Read `state` instead, since a false here does not tell measured absence from could-not-establish.

note.description: Why, when the requirement is unsatisfied or inapplicable, telling a constituent measured absent from one that could not be established. On `fhardened-effective`'s `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE` slot it is present in every state and names the reading that set the bar, or why none was set; `bar` carries the same as values.

implementation.description: The C library's fortify implementation the `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE` slot was read under, present where one of `fortify-effective`'s fortify-headers clauses decided its reading (Alpine, Chimera). fortify-headers implements level 1 whatever is requested, so the slot reads `in-force` where `requested_level` meets the bar, with a note saying so, and the constituent's `level` stays the library's 1.

name.description: The implementation `fortify-effective`'s deciding clause identifies, `fortify-headers` whichever of its two clauses decided (the observation's `evidence.decoded.clause`). An open vocabulary: a later implementation adds a name without a schema change.

top_level.description: The highest level the implementation enforces: `1`.

requested_level.description: The level `fortify-requested` read, verbatim, where that check is `on` or `partial`; absent otherwise, and then the request meets no bar.

bar.description: The `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` level `fhardened-effective`'s `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE` slot was held to and which reading set it, the values the `note` names in words; absent where no reading set a bar. The consistency rule `fhardened-fortify-slot-disagrees-with-inputs` recomputes it, with the slot's `state`, `level` and `implementation`, from `toolchain.fhardened_fortify`, `environment.libc`, `toolchain.target_triple` and the two fortify observations.

level.description: The level: where `source` is `driver`, the one the dump defined; where it is `library`, 3 from glibc 2.35 and 2 below it and on musl.

source.description: `driver`: the level this driver's own `-fhardened -O2` dump defined (`toolchain.fhardened_fortify.fortify_source`), which is what `-fhardened` asks of a build here. `library`: where the dump did not answer, as on a driver that refuses the option, the level gcc's `-fhardened` would ask on the C library `environment.libc` and `toolchain.target_triple` name, a statement about the option on this library rather than a reading of this compiler.

opt_out.description: A program header in the measured artifact by which the program opts out of what its marking asks for: OpenBSD's PT_OPENBSD_NOBTCFI, which `cfi-effective` alone reads (`facts[...].elf.openbsd_nobtcfi`). With it the constituent is `absent` where `environment.libc.impl` is `openbsd`, whose kernel was measured honouring it, and `not-established` for a marked artifact elsewhere, while `verdict` keeps the marking's own reading; `composite-verdict-disagrees-with-constituents` holds both to the store.

facts.description: The `facts` key of the artifact carrying the header: the cited observation's `build.artifact_sha256`.

state.description: `in-force` and `absent` are measured; `not-established` means the constituent could not be measured, so the umbrella cannot be confirmed; `not-applicable` drops out. `marked` means the check reads a marking the artifact carries (`cet-marked`, `branch-protection-marked`), a request for a protection whose enforcement the constituent does not measure: the reduction confirms it as it does `in-force`, the `note` says what the report measured of enforcement, and `cfi-effective`'s constituent and `fhardened-effective`'s `-fcf-protection=full` slot read `marked`, never `in-force`.

defect_coverage.description: A derived view keyed by the defect a flag protects against rather than by flag, which answers whether a given primitive is closed.

status.description: Read from the bearing checks that observe protection (`observations[].observes`); a request or marking moves it in no direction. `mitigated`: every bearing check decided, and each one observing protection read a full `on`, at least one; `partial`: some protection but not all; `not-mitigated`: protection observed absent and nowhere present, which needs only one decided check, so read `complete` beside it; `unknown`: no bearing check observed protection or its absence.

complete.description: Whether every bearing check produced a verdict, a request's or marking's own key counting as one; a consumer treating `not-mitigated` as a finding should require it. `true` beside `unknown` is a class only requests or markings bear (`jump-oriented-programming`): a gap in the corpus, not a finding.

verdict_counts.description: The bearing checks counted by verdict in protection terms: a weakening check's `off` counts as `on`, a request reads `requested` (on or partial) or `not-requested` (off), a marking `marked` or `not-marked`, and a withheld verdict keeps its name. This chard writes and accepts only the thirteen keys declared; the object stays open so a validator accepts a key a later chard adds.

coverage.description: Mandatory: what was fed, counted against the corpus, since a check never handed to the harness cannot report its own absence. `checks_expected` is what this run selected, and `corpus_checks_total` what exists.

checks_expected.description: Distinct check ids the selection named, reconciled with `observations` by id (`checks_missing`, `checks_unexpected`) as well as by count, since a list of the right length can measure one check twice and another not at all. In a report of this corpus, the selection is read back from `run.invocation`'s `--probe` values, and this count and both lists are held to it.

checks_attempted.description: The length of `observations`. Held equal to the `verdict_counts` total, and to the number of distinct check ids, by the `coverage-disagrees-with-observations` rule.

checks_valid.description: Observations whose control triple discriminated, the forced-on and forced-off arms reading apart, held to each `controls.discriminating` by `coverage-disagrees-with-observations`. A count of triples, not of measurements: it can exceed `withholding.published`, since the as-configured build can still give no reading, or a gating rule withhold the check.

checks_skipped.description: Expected ids with no observation, counted; `checks_missing` names them.

checks_missing.description: Check ids the selection named and no observation carries. Absent when empty, which is every healthy run.

checks_unexpected.description: Check ids an observation carries and the selection never named, absent when empty: a harness fault, recorded rather than refused when the report is written, which reads both completeness flags false. A report of this corpus carrying one is refused on read, since this binary measures the selected probes alone.

checks_not_applicable_here.description: Checks the target architecture puts out of reach: those the architecture gate withheld under `arch-gated`, each an earned limitation that settles `all_verdicts_published`, and not those `target-arch-contradicted` or `target-abi-contradicted` withhold. The gate reads the mechanism table, keyed on the question a check answers, and publishes `arch-gated` only where the target answers that question with another mechanism a check reads: on x86_64 branch-protection-macro, branch-protection-marked, gcs-macro, gcs-marked and pac-ret-enforced; on x86 branch-protection-macro, branch-protection-marked, gcs-macro and gcs-marked; on aarch64 cet-macro, cet-marked, cet-marked-object and cet-endbr-emitted. A check whose question the target answers with a mechanism no check reads there, its own or another (`no-check-on-target`), or that the table has no row for on the target (`arch-outside-table`), is withheld `indeterminate` with no `gating.arch` and is not counted here: on x86_64 bti-enforced; on x86 bti-enforced, pac-ret-enforced, shadow-stack-enforced, noexecstack-enforced, ubsan-trap-mode, fortify-printf-flag and zero-call-used-regs; on aarch64 shadow-stack-enforced and linker-default-noexecstack. `chard probes` lists each check's gate.

verdict_counts.description: Each verdict's count over all observations, summing to `checks_attempted` (held by `coverage-disagrees-with-observations`).

profile_flags_unexamined.description: Profile flags no observation in this report examines, in the profile's own spelling and order, absent when empty and named in `truncations` when not. A flag reaches a check's `flag` through a key (`-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE` reaches `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE`, a `-W` flag only itself, `--param` the parameter's name), and one whose only cell is `build-failed` or `probe-invalid` counts as examined, so an empty list does not say every flag has a verdict.

truncations.description: Anything deliberately capped, sampled, or dropped. Silent truncation reads as full coverage; it must be recorded here.

gate.description: What `measure --fail-on-missing` was allowed to excuse and what it excused, present on every run under that flag and absent otherwise, with both lists written when empty. Whether the gate passed is the exit status's to say; an excused check is still withheld, and `all_verdicts_published` stays false.

allowed.description: The gating rules `--allow` named, each once. `no-check-on-target` is the only rule it takes: it withholds a mechanism chard does not read on the target, which is the same on every machine and toolchain of that target.

rule.description: The allowed rule that held the check, its `gating.rule`.

excused.description: Each observation an allowance excused from the gate, sorted by check id: withheld `indeterminate` under a rule `allowed` names. A pipeline that holds the set fixed diffs this list.

corpus_checks_total.description: Total checks in the embedded corpus, whatever the `--probe` filter, against which both completeness flags are judged, so a filtered run cannot report itself complete. Held on read to this binary's count in a report of this corpus, and the report's own word in a report of another.

all_checks_attempted.description: Every corpus check was attempted under its own id: `checks_attempted` equals `corpus_checks_total`, and `checks_missing` and `checks_unexpected` are both empty, held by `coverage-disagrees-with-observations` when written and when read. Attempting a check is not answering it, so this can read true beside `probe-invalid` verdicts.

all_verdicts_published.description: Every corpus check was attempted under its own id and settled, as a measurement (`on`, `off`, `partial`) or an earned limitation: `all_checks_attempted` with `withholding.instrument_withholdings` empty, the claim `--fail-on-missing` gates on, which says the run was complete and not that the build is hardened. A check withheld under `no-check-on-target` or `arch-outside-table` is an instrument withholding, so on a target with a mechanism no check reads (x86_64, x86, aarch64) or no table row this is false, and `--fail-on-missing` fails unless `--allow no-check-on-target` excuses those checks. No allowance excuses `arch-outside-table`.

evidence_filters.description: What the per-observation evidence was trimmed to, by field. Mandatory: a filter a report does not name is a reader told the evidence is complete.

macros.description: The name list every macro-channel observation's `evidence.macros` is trimmed to, cited by digest as `evidence.macros_filter`: a macro absent from `evidence.macros` is undefined or outside this list, which is what tells the two apart. `--emit-macros` keeps the full dump once, under `toolchain.predefined_macros`.

symbols.description: The names the ELF reader looks for in a symbol table, which are all a stored `elf.watched_symbols` holds, so a name outside the list is one the reader never looked for rather than one the artifact lacks.

consistency.description: Whether this report's derived fields (`fortify_ratchet`, `defect_coverage`, `composites`) and the claims beside them agree with the observations under them, and which rules checked them. A contradiction is a fault in chard, or an `--execution` the run contradicts, never a finding about the toolchain.

status.description: `contradicted` when `contradictions` holds an entry and `consistent` when it holds none, as strong as `rules_applied` and `fields_checked` say. A `contradicted` report never reaches the requested path or stdout: it is written to `<file>.contradicted` beside the regular file it would have gone to, the default file included, and kept nowhere when `-o` names stdout, a device or a FIFO.

rules_applied.description: The ids of the rules the consistency pass ran, in the order it ran them: a rule is named when its step runs, even over nothing it reads, so a rule not named did not run. `table`, `matrix` and `digest` re-run on read the rules that need nothing outside the file, and some hold a report of another chard revision or probe corpus only to the keys it carries. `derived-fortify-level-exceeds-measured`: `fortify_ratchet` is not the one its rung observations give, or derives a level above the one the C library settled on. `dynamic-bounds-without-whole-object-bounds`: the ratchet reports dynamic bounds with no whole-object bounds. `defect-status-disagrees-with-bearing-checks`: a `defect_coverage` entry's `status`, `complete` or counts are not a recount of the observations bearing its defect. `composite-verdict-disagrees-with-constituents`: an umbrella's verdict, or a constituent's state or `applicable`, is not the one its constituents give. `fhardened-fortify-slot-disagrees-with-inputs`: `fhardened-effective`'s `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE` slot is not the one the toolchain, the C library, the target and the fortify observations give. `fhardened-ssp-slot-disagrees-with-input`: its `-fstack-protector-strong` slot is not the one the `ssp-level-emitted` observation gives. `asserted-execution-mode-contradicted-by-observation`: the operator's `--execution` and what chard observed disagree. `withholding-disagrees-with-verdict-counts`: `coverage.withholding` and the verdict tally count the same observations differently. `coverage-disagrees-with-observations`: the coverage counts and id lists do not describe the observations and the invocation's selection. `run-id-disagrees-with-measurement`: `run.inputs_sha256` or `run.id`, recomputed from the report, differs from the published value. `gating-rule-reserves-a-different-verdict`: an observation's verdict is not the one its `gating.rule` publishes. `runtime-reading-disagrees-with-its-run`: a runtime observation's verdict or gating does not fit its run: output cut or unreadable, the deadline, or emulation. `kernel-gate-disagrees-with-execution-mode`: a `needs_vm` check's verdict or gating is not the one the execution mode reserves; it reads the corpus, so it runs at publish only. `kernel-ownership-disagrees-with-execution-mode`: `environment.kernel`'s `is_host_kernel` or `ownership` is not the one `execution.mode` and its basis give. `arch-gate-contradicted-by-artifacts`: `toolchain.target` is not what the builds' ELF headers and macro dumps give, or an arch-gated observation they contradict is not withheld. `structured-diagnostics-disagrees-with-observations`: the `structured_diagnostics` summary is not the count of the observations' comparisons. `verdict-unearned-by-controls`: an observation's verdict or gating does not fit its control triple. `level-disagrees-with-check-scale`: a `level` or `recommended_level` does not fit the verdict or the check's scale. `gating-rejection-absent-from-arm-stderr`: a gating that rests on a tool's own sentence (`flag-unknown-to-driver`, `flag-refused-by-driver`, `unhardened-state-unbuildable`, `linker-keyword-ignored`, `scaffolding-unbuildable`) quotes a line its arm's `build.stderr` does not carry. `build-rejection-disagrees-with-build-stderr`: `build_rejection` is not the rejection its own `build.stderr` gives, or stands beside a verdict other than `build-failed`. `corroboration-disagrees-with-members`: a corroboration group is not the one its member observations give. `fact-store-disagrees-with-references`: `facts` and the digests that reference it disagree, or a stored artifact was built by another compiler than `toolchain` names. `decoded-reading-disagrees-with-facts`: a decoded reading, re-evaluated over the facts it names, does not give its published clause, outcome, level or verdict; `replay` counts what it fed itself. `cxx-assertions-derived-from-inputs`: `evidence.cxx_assertions_source` is not the one the build's macros and the profile's C++ flags give. `profile-flag-rejection-disagrees-with-observations`: the `profile-flag-rejected` diagnostics are not one per tool and flag the `build-failed` observations' builds refuse. `digest-disagrees-with-report`: `digest` or `profile.flags_sha256` is not the one the report's own fields give. `macro-verdict-unearned-by-artifact`: a macro-channel measurement stands over an artifact that gave no account of its macros. `macro-verdict-contradicted-by-artifact`: a macro-channel measurement reads the opposite presence to a check that reads the same protection from the artifact or a run of it.

fields_checked.description: The fields the rules examined; a field absent from this list was not checked, whatever `contradictions` says.

contradictions.description: The claims in this report that contradict others in it; always present, and `[]` when the rules in `rules_applied` found none.

rule.description: The stable id of the rule that fired, as `rules_applied` describes it, so a consumer can gate on a class rather than on prose.

property.description: The property both claims are about.

replay.description: What `decoded-reading-disagrees-with-facts` fed itself against what it replayed: `readings` is `replayed + unresolved` plus the length of `not_replayable`.

replayed.description: Re-evaluated with the Published view and compared.

unresolved.description: Not evaluated because a `facts` key or entry, or the check's `decoders` entry, is missing or of the wrong kind, or evaluated to a key the facts do not hold; each is named by a contradiction.

not_replayable.description: Readings the Published view stopped at a name `evidence_filters.macros` does not keep, reached by a `c-int` term following a mode value, as with `-D_LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE=MYMODE -DMYMODE=4`. Not a contradiction: the trimmed map says nothing about that name.

diagnostics.description: Harness-level problems not attributable to a single probe. One with the context `profile-flag-rejected` carries `rejection`, one per program and profile flag it refused (a flag gcc and g++ both refuse is two), and those come first, the most `cells_withheld` first, then by tool and flag.

rejection.description: Present only on a `profile-flag-rejected` warning: one tool and one profile flag it refused, counted over the `build-failed` observations whose published build it refused that flag in, on any refusal line. It says whose flag it was and what the tool said, not whether the flag is misspelt or newer than the toolchain, and the `profile-flag-rejection-disagrees-with-observations` consistency rule recomputes it.

tool.description: The program the refusal line names (`gcc`, `g++`, `clang`, `cc1`, a linker's path), or `the toolchain` where the line opens with none.

flag.description: The profile flag refused, as the tool spelled it: a linker names `--no-such-option` for a profile's `-Wl,--no-such-option`.

supplied_by.description: `built-in-profile`: a profile chard builds, named by `profile.id`, supplied the flag. `operator`: under `--profile explicit`, the operator's `--flags`, `--cxxflags` or `--ldflags` supplied it.

line.description: The line the build of the observation `first_check` names refused the flag on, as published in `build.stderr`, relative to the work directory.

first_check.description: The first observation, in report order, whose published build this tool refused this flag in.

cells_withheld.description: The `build-failed` observations whose published build this tool refused this flag in.

cells_attempted.description: Every observation in the report, `coverage.checks_attempted`: the frame for `cells_withheld`.

listings.description: One probe's answers. Each comparison is present exactly where the probe owes it under the report's profile; within one, an answer after the first that could not be read is absent, since nothing after it was asked.

link.description: `link-inputs-unmatched-by-arms`: the measured link's listing and, where it was read, the arms' selection's under its linkage form.

clean_link.description: `clean-link-unmatched-by-measured`: the measured link's listing, the clean build's link listing under the measured line's linker selection (`footing`), and the two `-print-search-dirs` answers, in the order asked.

compile.description: `compile-inputs-unmatched-by-arms`: the measured compile's listing, the stand-in's, and one listing per arm optimisation class, asked only where the first two were read and agree.

measured_compile.description: The measured compile's listing, whose sanitizer and LTO words the sanitizer rules and `lto-codegen-at-link` read.

paths.description: What the comparisons read of the filesystem, keyed by each path as the listing wrote it: its canonical absolute path (the path itself where it does not resolve) and whether it is a directory. A replay reads these in place of a filesystem, and cannot replay a record that lacks a path a comparison reads.

asked_link.description: One question put to the driver: the flags it was asked under, as asked, and either its link line's inputs or `error`, the sentence saying why it could not be read.

asked_search_dirs.description: One question put to the driver: the flags it was asked under, as asked, and either its search lists or `error`, the sentence saying why it could not be read.

asked_compile.description: One question put to the driver: the flags it was asked under, as asked, and either its compile commands' inputs or `error`, the sentence saying why it could not be read.

link_inputs.description: What one `-###` link line combines beyond the program's own objects.

search_dirs.description: The `programs:` and `libraries:` lists of a `-print-search-dirs` answer, in order.

compile_inputs.description: What the compile commands of one `-###` listing read beyond the probe's source.

linker.description: The linker the profile links with, read from the driver's `-###` link line under the profile's `-fuse-ld=`, `--ld-path=` and `-B` flags, or from `-print-prog-name` where that line names no link. Every published report carries `artifact`, the linked artifacts' check of that identity.

version.description: First line of the linker's own --version output. Absent where it printed none or the job did not exit 0 with its output whole; `kind` is then `unknown`, and `detection` says how the job ended.

path.description: The linker's absolute path; a bare name the driver prints is resolved on PATH, as the driver's own link step would. Absent where it could not be resolved, and `detection` says why.

path_source.description: Who turned the name into `path`: `driver`, the driver printed it; `path-search`, the driver printed a bare name and chard searched PATH; `profile`, the profile named the file through `--ld-path=` or `-fuse-ld=/path`. Present exactly when `path` is.

profile_flags.description: The profile flags consulted, as written: `-B` prefixes, `-fuse-ld=` and `--ld-path=`. Absent when the profile selected nothing and the driver's default is the linker reported.

detection.description: How the linker was identified, in prose: the query the driver was asked, what it printed, and who resolved it.

artifact.description: The linked artifacts' testimony against `kind`, read from the line lld and mold write to `.comment`; GNU ld and gold write none, so a `bfd` or `gold` banner can at most be uncontradicted. `kind` stays the banner's word, and a consumer that needs the artifacts' answer gates on `agreement`.

agreement.description: `agrees`: every linked artifact carries one linker line, naming the banner's kind and version. `disagrees`: the artifacts name another linker or version, or two linkers, or the banner names lld or mold and no artifact carries its line; an error diagnostic under `toolchain.linker`, not a contradiction. `artifact-only`: every linked artifact carries one linker line, and no banner chard read names a linker (`kind` is `unknown`); a warning diagnostic. `no-signature`: no artifact carries a linker line, and the banner names GNU ld, gold or no linker chard recognises. `no-linked-artifact`: nothing was counted, `artifacts_read` is 0, and `evidence` opens with why.

signature.description: The `.comment` line that named a linker, when one did.

artifacts_read.description: Distinct linked artifacts, by `build.artifact_sha256`, whose `.comment` was read to its end. Relocatables, unreadable `.comment` sections and clean builds linked without the profile's linker selection are named in `evidence` and not counted.

evidence.description: Which artifacts, what their `.comment` carried, and why the verdict follows: on `disagrees`, the first disagreeing pair and the count of the rest; then the artifacts left uncounted, each under its reason, and the probes that contributed no readable artifact.

cxx.description: The linker the C++ probes were linked with, queried through the C++ driver, present only where the cxxflags select a different one from the C link and a C++ driver exists. Its `artifact` is held to the C++ probes' artifacts alone, and it never carries a `cxx` of its own.

verdict.description: `off` is a positive claim requiring proof that the observable would have appeared; it is never the default for a failed measurement.

argv.description: The full compiler invocation, run in the work directory and re-runnable from inside it. Every path under that directory is recorded relative to it: `-o probe` here was `-o <workdir>/probe` at the driver.

dropped_flags.description: Profile flags removed before this build because they cannot coexist with the probe's output kind, such as `-pie` against `-shared`: what reconciles `profile.cflags` with `argv`. Absent when nothing was removed.

stderr.description: The compiler's diagnostics, truncated: the observable of the compiler-diag channel. Paths under the work directory are relative to it and a compiler's temporary objects read `<compiler-temp>` in this published copy only; the detectors read the stream as captured.

stdout.description: The job's standard output. On a `-dM -E` dump record (`evidence.macro_dump`, the arms' `macro_dump`) the defines are replaced by a line giving their count; `evidence.macros` carries the filtered map and `--emit-macros` keeps the toolchain's dump.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock lifetime of the child process in whole milliseconds; `0` means under a millisecond, not untimed.

stdout_unterminated.description: Present, and true, where standard output ended partway through a line, read before `stdout` was trimmed; absent otherwise. On a `-dM -E` dump record it means the dump was cut off whatever its exit status, so its last line is not read as a define and the dump is read as failed wherever it is read.

stdout_sha256.description: On a `-dM -E` dump record, the SHA-256 of standard output with its lines sorted bytewise and joined by newlines, no newline after the last (`LC_ALL=C sort` with the final newline removed): the key of the dump's `macro-dump` entry in `facts`. Sorted so that it moves only where a line does, since gcc's listing order can change with no macro changed.

exit_status.description: -1 when the process did not exit normally; see `signal`.

signal.description: The terminating signal's name (SIGABRT, SIGSEGV), resolved on the host that ran the probe. A trap instruction reads SIGILL on x86_64 (`ud2`) and SIGTRAP on aarch64 (`brk`).

stdout.description: The probe's standard output. On Darwin a probe whose reading rests on the machine opens it with a `CHARD-TRANSLATION` line (`0`, `1`, or `unreadable` with the failure), which `run-under-emulation` reads; a reading that varies between runs is listed under `x-volatile-readings`, and under --normalize its digits read `<volatile>` here, in the check's `evidence.observed` and in its arms' `detail`.

stderr.description: Where glibc's "*** buffer overflow detected ***" and friends land.

timed_out.description: Whether `deadline_ms` elapsed before chard saw the probe exit. A probe that exited before the kill keeps its status and is read; one the kill ended (`signal` `SIGKILL`, or no status) is withheld under `run-deadline-elapsed`.

deadline_ms.description: The deadline this run was held to, in whole milliseconds: `--timeout`, the same value as `run.deadlines.probe_run_ms`.

output_error.description: Why an output stream could not be read; absent on every healthy run. Present, an empty `stdout` or `stderr` is chard's failure to read it and not the probe's silence, so no verdict is read from it and a runtime check over the run is withheld under `run-output-unreadable`.

output_truncated.description: A stream reached the 16 KiB capture cap and lost its tail. A runtime check over the run is withheld under `run-output-unreadable`, and a control arm over one reads `indeterminate` with the cut named in its `detail`.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock lifetime of the child process in whole milliseconds; `0` means under a millisecond, not untimed.

environment.description: The complete environment the probe received, name to value: the pins every probe receives and those it declares (`run_environment` in `chard probes`), with no ambient variable. A reader re-deriving a runtime verdict runs the artifact under this map alone.

symbol_fact.description: One symbol-table entry, reduced to what a detector asks about, under the key `watched_symbols` describes.

defined.description: false is SHN_UNDEF, a reference satisfied at load time: a canary-protected binary references __stack_chk_fail, and one that statically links libssp defines it.

tables.description: The symbol tables that carried the name: `.symtab` and `.dynsym`, or `SHT_SYMTAB` and `SHT_DYNSYM` where a table's name could not be read. A stripped binary has only `.dynsym`, so an absent symbol there is weaker evidence.

versioned.description: The versioned spellings `.symtab` stored (`__stack_chk_fail@GLIBC_2.4`, or `name@@VERSION` for a default version), which the key cuts. Absent when every table stored the name bare.

fact_entry.description: One entry of `facts`, tagged by `kind`: `elf`, an artifact the reader accepted, its account as `chard elf` prints it except that a member a predicate reads is stated as `[]` or `null` where `chard elf` omits it; `unreadable`, an artifact that linked and that the reader refused or `measure` set aside, with `error` (its path read as `<artifact>`, and a set-aside one's opening `set aside unread:`) and `mach_o`, true where the reader refused a Mach-O object; `elf-delta`, an arm's accepted artifact stated as `elf_changes` against `base`; `macro-dump`, a `-dM -E` dump with `defines`, `macros_filter` and `macros`. Each kind carries exactly its own members, which this schema, declaring their union, does not enforce.

base.description: The key of the `elf` entry an `elf-delta` is stated against: an observation's own `build.artifact_sha256`.

elf_changes.description: The members of `$defs/elf_facts`, as serialized, whose values in the arm's facts differ from `base`'s; the arm's facts are the base's with these in place. A member the base carries and the arm omits is stated as its empty list or map (`openbsd_nobtcfi` as `false`) and resolves to the member's absence, never to the empty value.

defines.description: How many `#define` lines the dump printed: the count its published record's `stdout` names.

macros_filter.description: `evidence_filters.macros.sha256`: the filter `macros` was trimmed through, the same one an observation's inline `evidence.macros` passes through.

macros.description: The dump's defines that survive the filter, name to value (empty string when defined with no value).

elf_facts.description: Everything the elf-static channel reads from one artifact: the header, the link classification, the dynamic section, the property markings, the symbols and the recorded strings. The nine nullable link facts (`pie`, `static_pie`, `shared_object`, `statically_linked`, `relro`, `gnu_relro`, `bind_now`, `gnu_stack_present`, `gnu_stack_executable`) are `null` together on an object the loader cannot run, and carry a value together on every ET_EXEC and ET_DYN.

elf_class.description: EI_CLASS, the width in bits of the file's addresses and offsets. With `elf_data` it is what `toolchain.target.abi` holds the artifact to.

elf_data.description: EI_DATA, the byte order the file was read in, which tells `ppc64` from ppc64le and `aarch64` from aarch64_be. A record without it is left out of `toolchain.target.abi.artifacts`, and the execution witness withholds on it.

elf_type.description: e_type by name: ET_NONE, ET_REL, ET_EXEC, ET_DYN or ET_CORE. Any other value reads `unrecognised (e_type 0x..)`, with `OS-specific` or `processor-specific` before `e_type` where the value falls in that range.

machine.description: e_machine as the family's short name: i386, mips, ppc, ppc64, s390, arm, x86_64, aarch64, riscv or loongarch. Any other value reads `unrecognised (e_machine 0x..)`. Width and byte order are `elf_class` and `elf_data`.

has_interp.description: A PT_INTERP segment names a loader.

has_dynamic.description: The dynamic section was found and carries at least one entry.

pie.description: ET_DYN plus DF_1_PIE, a PT_INTERP or a DT_DEBUG entry, since ET_DYN alone cannot tell a PIE from a shared library. `null`, as are the eight nullable link facts after it, on an object the loader cannot run, and a check reading `null` is withheld: `indeterminate`, or `not-applicable` under `artifact-cannot-carry-observable` where the artifact fails the check's precondition.

df_1_pie.description: DF_1_PIE in DT_FLAGS_1, the linker's own record of a PIE link; false on an object with no dynamic flags.

static_pie.description: ET_DYN with no interpreter and DF_1_PIE or DT_DEBUG, either of which marks executable output; without one it is an ordinary shared library, and DT_SONAME does not override the mark. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

shared_object.description: ET_DYN with a dynamic section, no interpreter, and neither DF_1_PIE nor DT_DEBUG. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

statically_linked.description: No loader runs it: an ET_EXEC with no interpreter, a static PIE, or an ET_DYN with neither an interpreter nor a dynamic section. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

relro.description: `full` is a PT_GNU_RELRO segment with `bind_now`, `partial` the segment without it, `none` no segment. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

gnu_relro.description: A PT_GNU_RELRO segment is present. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

bind_now.description: Immediate binding under any of its three spellings: a DT_BIND_NOW entry, DF_BIND_NOW in DT_FLAGS, or DF_1_NOW in DT_FLAGS_1. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

gnu_stack_present.description: A PT_GNU_STACK segment is present; a missing one defers to the kernel's default, which a detector reads as unmeasured rather than as a non-executable stack. `null` under the rule stated on `pie`.

gnu_stack_executable.description: PF_X on the last PT_GNU_STACK segment, the one Linux acts on; false when `gnu_stack_present` is false, and `null` under the rule stated on `pie`. Where two such segments disagree on PF_X, `truncations` carries an `unread` `gnu-stack` entry, which withholds `noexecstack` and `linker-default-noexecstack` alone.

rwx_segment.description: A PT_LOAD or PT_TLS segment carries both PF_W and PF_X; `rwx-segment-absent` reads `true` as `on`, the adverse finding, and `false` as `off`, the protected state. A report's stored facts state `null` where there is no linked object, and the check withholds over `null` or a missing member rather than read either as `off`.

df_1_noopen.description: DF_1_NOOPEN in DT_FLAGS_1, the linker's record of `-z nodlopen`.

textrel.description: DF_TEXTREL in DT_FLAGS or a standalone DT_TEXTREL entry; both are read because bfd writes DT_FLAGS only when it is non-zero.

dt_relr.description: A DT_RELR entry: relative relocations in the packed format.

dt_debug.description: A DT_DEBUG entry, the linker's mark of executable output and the third marker `pie` and `static_pie` accept beside DF_1_PIE and PT_INTERP. False on an object with no dynamic section.

dt_soname.description: A DT_SONAME entry, recorded and not consulted by the classification: DT_DEBUG beside DT_SONAME is still executable output.

dynamic_tags.description: Every (tag, value) pair in the dynamic section, in file order, each as `0x<tag>=0x<value>` in lowercase hex, so a verdict that turns on one flag bit is auditable from the report alone. Empty when there is no dynamic section.

needed.description: Every DT_NEEDED string, resolved through the DT_STRTAB the dynamic section names, in dynamic-section order.

gnu_property_types.description: Every property type in the object's NT_GNU_PROPERTY_TYPE_0 notes, whatever the machine, ascending, each as `0x` and eight lowercase hex digits (`0xc0000002` is the x86 feature word, `0xc0000000` the aarch64 one). The five feature bits below are decoded only on the machine that defines the type.

gnu_property_notes.description: How many notes carried each type in `gnu_property_types`, present only when at least one property note exists. A linker writes each type once, so a count of two is a file no linker wrote, and its feature bits are the AND of both notes.

x86_ibt.description: The IBT bit of GNU_PROPERTY_X86_FEATURE_1_AND, decoded on an x86 object only. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

x86_shstk.description: The SHSTK bit of GNU_PROPERTY_X86_FEATURE_1_AND, decoded on an x86 object only. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

aarch64_bti.description: The BTI bit of GNU_PROPERTY_AARCH64_FEATURE_1_AND on an aarch64 object, or on an `ET_REL` without that note the `Tag_Feature_BTI` build attribute gcc 16 with binutils 2.46 writes in its place; where both disagree, the bit is their AND and `truncations` records `notes` unread. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

aarch64_pac.description: The PAC bit of GNU_PROPERTY_AARCH64_FEATURE_1_AND on an aarch64 object, or on an `ET_REL` without that note the `Tag_Feature_PAC` build attribute gcc 16 with binutils 2.46 writes in its place; where both disagree, the bit is their AND and `truncations` records `notes` unread. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

aarch64_gcs.description: The GCS bit of GNU_PROPERTY_AARCH64_FEATURE_1_AND on an aarch64 object, or on an `ET_REL` without that note the `Tag_Feature_GCS` build attribute gcc 16 with binutils 2.46 writes in its place; where both disagree, the bit is their AND and `truncations` records `notes` unread. A marking and no more: whether it is enforced is the CPU's and the kernel's.

openbsd_nobtcfi.description: A PT_OPENBSD_NOBTCFI program header (0x65a3dbe8), which lld writes under `-z nobtcfi` for any target: the program's request that OpenBSD not enforce branch-target CFI (BTI on arm64, IBT on amd64) on it. Present only when true; `cfi-effective` reads it.

sections.description: Section names as the name table stores them, in header order, with empty names dropped. Empty when the object has no section-header table or its name table could not be read, which `truncations` records.

data_in_code_pages.description: The allocated sections without SHF_EXECINSTR, `.note.gnu.build-id` aside, whose bytes lie in a page an executable PT_LOAD maps (the segment's p_align, at least 4096 bytes), in header order, a section with no readable name as its index in brackets; empty is the layout `-z separate-code` asks for, and `separate-code` reads it. `null`, which a report's `facts` store states, where no PT_LOAD carries PF_X or no section header describes an allocated section.

code_relocations.description: On a relocatable object, the distinct relocations applied to code, sorted, each as the `readelf -r` type (or `reloc-type-` and its hex number), a space, the symbol's name or a section's in brackets (`R_X86_64_PC32 [.data]`), and a non-default visibility as a third word (`R_386_PC32 __x86.get_pc_thunk.ax STV_HIDDEN`). `null`, which a report's `facts` store states, for anything but an ET_REL with a section-header table; `plt-bypassed` and `pic-object-relocs` read it.

function_references.description: For a relocatable object, each defined STT_FUNC symbol in symbol-table order as `name:`, then `name:target` for each distinct named symbol a relocation inside the function's range refers to, sorted, and after the functions `?:target` for each one code outside every function refers to. `null`, which a report's `facts` store states, where the object is not relocatable, has no SHT_SYMTAB or is a 64-bit MIPS object; `ssp-level-emitted` reads it, and a relocation section the reader could not finish is a `relocations` truncation.

symbol_tables.description: The symbol tables the file has, in header order: `.symtab` and `.dynsym`, or `SHT_SYMTAB` and `SHT_DYNSYM` where the section names could not be read. Absent when there are none, as in a stripped static link, where `canary-emitted`, `ssp-covers-small-arrays` and `cxx-assertions-symbol` read `not-applicable` under `artifact-cannot-carry-observable`; a table the reader could not reach is in `truncations` instead.

symbol_count.description: Distinct symbol names across every symbol table read, keyed as `watched_symbols` is, so a versioned and a bare spelling of one name count once.

watched_symbols.description: The symbols detectors ask about, each present only when a table carried it, keyed on a `.symtab` name before its first `@` and a `.dynsym` name whole. An absent name was found in no table that was read, and `truncations` says whether a table went unread.

table.description: The ELF table the reader could not finish; no entry names `header` or `program-headers`, since the reader refuses such a file and the observation is withheld. `gnu-stack` is two PT_GNU_STACK headers that disagree on PF_X, `section-headers` a section-header table the file declares and the reader could not read, `code` a scanned function's bytes, and `relocations` a code relocation section of a relocatable object, which `code_relocations` then lists in part.

kind.description: `unread`: the table's facts could not be read, and a check declaring the table is withheld under `artifact-unreadable`. `ignored`: a view of the table that disagreed with the loader's was dropped and the loader's view measured, so the facts are whole and no check is withheld.

detail.description: The reader's own sentence, with the offset or index it stopped at, which gating reasons and diagnostics quote.

truncations.description: Tables this parse could not read to their end, each typed by table and by what the cut did to the facts, so a fact measured absent is told from one not read. Always present in a `facts` entry of kind `elf`, `[]` included, and in an `elf-delta` where the arm's differs from its base's; absent when empty in `chard elf` output.

comment.description: Distinct lines of the artifact's `.comment` section, in file order, one from each producer that writes one: the compiler, lld and mold, and not GNU ld or gold. Absent when the section is missing or empty; one that could not be read names itself in `truncations`.

function_entries.description: `<function>=<hex>`, in file order, for each function whose entry chard reads that the object defines in `.symtab`: its first four bytes in lowercase hex, fewer where its `st_size` is smaller; `cet-endbr-emitted` reads it. Stated in an `elf` entry of a report's `facts` store, `[]` included, and a listed function that could not be read is a `function-entries` truncation.

run_witness.description: The run nonces the artifact carries, each as thirty-two lowercase hex digits, from the type-1 `chard` notes of a `.note.chard.run` section or, where the file shows none, a `PT_NOTE` segment; each distinct value once, in file order, at most four. A report stores an artifact as `elf` only where this list is exactly `run.artifact_witness.nonce`, which is checked at publication and not when a report is read back; absent on a file no chard run built and on every macOS artifact.

self_report.description: Contents of the `.chard.report` section, the artifact's own account of its macros, which the other channels cross-check: a `CHARD-REPORT-V2` line, `NAME=value` or `NAME undefined` per macro, and `CHARD-REPORT-END`. Empty when the section is absent; under a `CHARD-REPORT-V1` header, `NAME=?` reads as undefined.

recorded_command_line.description: Contents of `.GCC.command.line`, the driver command line where the toolchain was asked to record it (`-frecord-gcc-switches`, clang's `-frecord-command-line`); empty when the section is absent.
