It holds no default compiled into the compiler, so it complements the macro channel.

code_scanned.description: `<function>:<pattern>=<count>`, zero counts included, for each byte pattern of the artifact's machine searched in a function chard scans whose bytes were read whole, so the list says what was searched; a fixed-pattern byte search, not a disassembly. Always present in a `facts` entry of kind `elf`, `[]` included, and a scanned function that could not be read is a `code` truncation.

code_matches.description: `<function>:<pattern>@<offset>` for each match `code_scanned` counts, the offset from the function's first byte, up to a fixed bound per function and pattern. Present in an `elf` entry as `code_scanned` is.

controls.description: The self-validation triple. Without a discriminating control pair, an absent observable means nothing.

flags.description: Exactly the check's declared positive control list, with no profile flag; fixed when the triple is decided.

build.description: What the arm compiled and how the compile ended, on every arm that was built.

run.description: What the arm's artifact did when it was run. Absent on the macro, `elf-static` and `compiler-diag` channels, where no arm is executed, and on a runtime arm whose build failed.

outcome.description: What the arm showed of the observable; absent where the arm could not be built or run.

detail.description: What the detector observed for this arm, or, where `outcome` is absent, why the arm could not be evaluated. Paths under the work directory are relative to it and a compiler's temporary objects read `<compiler-temp>`; a quoted stream cut to its budget reads `[N chars omitted]` on each cut side, keeping the matched line and its neighbours on the compiler-diag channel and the stream's end elsewhere.

macro_source.description: Where a macro-channel arm's macros were read from, absent on every other arm: `compiled-artifact`, the artifact's `.chard.report` (the `facts` entry under `build.artifact_sha256`), or `preprocessor`, its `cc -dM -E` dump (the `macro-dump` entry under `macro_dump.stdout_sha256`).

macro_dump.description: The arm's own `cc -dM -E` job on a macro-channel check, its defines replaced by a count and their digest kept as `stdout_sha256`. Its exit status and stderr are the only account of a macro-channel `positive-unevaluable` or `negative-unevaluable`.

decoded.description: The predicate's reading of this arm, on every arm with an `outcome` of a macro or `elf-static` check; its `outcome` is the arm's.

overridden.description: What the compile command the driver lists under this arm's flags showed of the arm's flag. chard publishes it exactly where `withheld_because` is `positive-overridden`.

overridden_unread.description: Why the compile command the driver lists under this arm's flags could not be read (no listing, not one compile command, or a setting chard cannot read), where the triple withheld as `positive-silent` and the driver was asked. Never beside `overridden`.

flags.description: Exactly the check's declared negative control list, with no profile flag; fixed when the triple is decided. `[]` means the clean build stood in as the negative sample, for a check that declares no negative control.

Paths under the work directory are relative to it and a compiler's temporary objects read `<compiler-temp>`; a quoted stream cut to its budget reads `[N chars omitted]` on each cut side, keeping the matched line and its neighbours on the compiler-diag channel and the stream's end elsewhere.

overridden.description: What the compile command the driver lists under this arm's flags showed of the arm's flag. chard publishes it exactly where `withheld_because` is `negative-overridden`.

overridden_unread.description: Why the compile command the driver lists under this arm's flags could not be read (no listing, not one compile command, or a setting chard cannot read), where the triple withheld as `negative-also-shows` and the driver was asked. Never beside `overridden`.

flags.description: The measured profile's flags for the probe's language and its ldflags, then the check's declared negative control list; fixed when the triple is decided.

run.description: What the arm's artifact did when it was run. Absent on the macro, `elf-static` and `compiler-diag` channels, where no arm is executed, and on a runtime arm whose build failed.

Paths under the work directory are relative to it and a compiler's temporary objects read `<compiler-temp>`; a quoted stream cut to its budget reads `[N chars omitted]` on each cut side, keeping the matched line and its neighbours on the compiler-diag channel and the stream's end elsewhere.

macro_dump.description: The arm's own `cc -dM -E` job on a macro-channel check, its defines replaced by a count and their digest kept as `stdout_sha256`. Its exit status and stderr are the only account of a macro-channel `positive-unevaluable` or `negative-unevaluable`.

decoded.description: The predicate's reading of this arm, on every arm with an `outcome` of a macro or `elf-static` check; its `outcome` is the arm's.

regime_negative.description: The negative control re-run under the measured profile's own flags, since the profile-free arms cannot show that the measured build's signal is the flag's. Where it shows the observable, a co-enabled flag produces the signal and the verdict is withheld.

discriminating.description: positive showed the observable AND negative did not. When false the measurement verdict must be `probe-invalid`.

withheld_because.description: Why the triple licensed no verdict, as a named set open to values a later chard adds, beside the sentence in `failure_reason`; present exactly when `discriminating` is false. `negative-overridden` and `positive-overridden` are `negative-also-shows` and `positive-silent` where the driver's compile command under that arm's flags sets the arm's option otherwise (the arm's `overridden` holds both words), which does not show that the override is why the control misbehaved.

overridden.description: A control arm's flag and the other word for the same option in the compile command the driver lists (`-###`) under the arm's flags, stating neither what put the word there nor that it is why the arm misbehaved, and earning or withholding no verdict. The listing is not published: the driver for the probe's language, under `profile.compiler_environment`, lists it again given the arm's `flags` and `-### -x c /dev/null -c -o /dev/null` (`-x c++` for a C++ probe).

flag.description: The arm's own setting of the option: its last word of that option among the arm's `flags`.

by.description: The other setting of the option in the compile command: a later word as the command carries it (`-fstack-protector-strong` after `-fno-stack-protector`; a `-D` or `-U` joined to its operand), or, in clang's `-cc1` command of resolved settings, the word in place of the arm's or `-stack-protector N` (1 to 3) where `N` is not the arm's level. Spellings are compared, and no order between the settings is implied.

check.description: The check id within the probe, the unit a verdict attaches to. The enumeration is open: a report may carry an id a later chard adds, which a consumer reads by the observation's other fields.

flag.description: The canonical flag the check reports on, such as `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE`.

polarity.description: `harden`: presence is good. `weaken`: presence is bad (an RPATH or RUNPATH entry, a text relocation) and `off` is the protected state, so a renderer can colour a cell without knowing the flag.

level.description: The level the detector reported, a word of the check's own scale as `chard probes` lists it under `levels`, graded against `recommended_level` where that is present. Present only beside a measurement verdict, and absent rather than null where no level was established.

recommended_level.description: The level the OpenSSF guide recommends, on the check's own scale, against which `level` is graded. Present exactly where the check grades a level, and never null.

confidence.description: How directly the check's observable establishes the protection, fixed per check rather than per run. It is not a probability, and it is not derived from `channel` or `controls.discriminating`.

observable.description: Human-readable statement of what was looked at.

boundary.description: What the verdict leaves to the kernel, the CPU or the C library where the binary runs, or, for a check that ran a program, the host it ran on. Present only for a protection with such a dependency, so absence means nothing outside the file is required, not that the question went unconsidered.

establishes.description: What the verdict does establish, in the artifact.

requires_at_runtime.description: What must also hold where the binary runs, and which this report does not check.

defects.description: The ids of the defect classes the check's flag bears on, chard's own mapping rather than a cited one. Empty says the flag is not a mitigation.

observes.description: What the check's `on` is evidence of: `protection` (the mechanism, or its producer's own word for its state, such as `__SSP_STRONG__`), `request` (a macro the build supplied to ask for it, such as `_FORTIFY_SOURCE`) or `marking` (a note or macro for a mechanism a CPU enforces, whose enforcement the check does not observe). `defect_coverage` moves a status on `protection` alone, and a report without this field is refused on read.

evidence.description: The channel's raw evidence, enough to re-derive the verdict without a rerun. The observation's ELF facts are its `facts` entry under `build.artifact_sha256`, not this block.

macros_filter.description: The SHA-256 of the name list `macros` was trimmed to, which `evidence_filters.macros` carries in full. Present exactly when `macros` is.

macro_source.description: Where `macros` was read from: the probe's own `.chard.report` section, or the `cc -dM -E` dump when the artifact carried none. Present on macro-channel observations only.

macro_dump.description: The record of the `cc -dM -E` job over the probe's translation unit under its build's compile words, on every macro-channel observation, with its defines replaced by their count. A dump that exited non-zero, defined nothing or was cut off partway through a line (`stdout_unterminated`) withholds every verdict read through it, and `observed` says which.

observed.description: What the detector saw, in one line, or why the channel could not be read when the verdict was withheld before any detector ran.

decoded.description: The predicate's reading of the measured build, on every observation of a macro or `elf-static` check that reached its decoder. An ungated `on`, `off` or `partial` is the verdict this reading gives on the check's scale: `absent` is `off`, `present` is `on`, or on a graded check `on` or `partial` by the level.

lto_pic.description: Why an `on` of `pic-shared-link` stood under link-time optimization: the measured compile's `-###` command resolved it to position-independent code without PIE, so `lto-codegen-at-link` did not withhold it. `lto` is the listing's last LTO word and `relocation` its code-model words, each once; absent on every other observation.

cxx_assertions_source.description: The label chard derives for the source of libstdc++'s assertions in the measured build, on the three checks that read them, from the build's published macros and the profile's C++ flags. `profile`: the flags define `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` or `_GLIBCXX_DEBUG`. `library-unoptimized-default`: the flags define neither and leave `_GLIBCXX_NO_ASSERTIONS` undefined, the build has no `__OPTIMIZE__`, and the flags carry no preprocessor input chard does not read (a forced include, a response file, a `-Xclang` define or undefine). libstdc++ 15 and 16 define the assertions themselves in such a build, and the label is named for that default. libstdc++ 13 and 14 have no such default. The derivation reads neither the library's release nor a define from outside the profile's flags, so an unoptimized build whose assertions come from a driver wrapper, a spec file, a variable given by `--env` or a flag that implies the define (gcc's `-fhardened`) can read this label too, over libstdc++ 13 and 14 as well. To learn whether the library has the default, take its release from the toolchain's libstdc++ headers: `__GLIBCXX__` in the macros is a date, not the release. `unattributed`: neither holds. Absent where `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` is undefined, the library is not libstdc++ or no triple was built; the verdicts do not depend on it.

gating.description: Why a check was withheld by a named rule rather than read `off`; the rule's premise fixes the one verdict it publishes. A fact about the measured system (its toolchain, target, C library or kernel) publishes `unsupported`: `arch-gated`, `libc-declared`, `compiler-declared`, `flag-unknown-to-driver`, `flag-refused-by-driver`, `linker-keyword-ignored`, `fortify-level-declined`, `link-drops-marking`, `subobject-bound-lost-in-wrapper`, `kernel-lacks-shadow-stack`. A limit of chard's instrument publishes `indeterminate`: `needs-vm`, `execution-mode-assumed`, `no-check-on-target`, `arch-outside-table`, `unhardened-state-unbuildable`, `scaffolding-unbuildable`, `macro-supplied-by-profile`, `no-driver`, `probe-unmeasured`, `artifact-unreadable`, `artifact-holds-lto-ir`, `artifact-lacks-self-report`, `artifact-lacks-run-witness`, `artifact-compiled-by-another-compiler`, `artifact-contradicts-link-mode`, `level-outside-check-scale`, `guard-kept-without-the-flag`, `unoptimized-build-cannot-show`, `fortify-below-the-subobject-level`, `canary-not-asked-for`, `frame-reuse-did-not-hold`, `run-output-unreadable`, `run-deadline-elapsed`, `run-under-emulation`, `target-arch-contradicted`, `target-abi-contradicted`, `cpu-lacks-shadow-stack`, `machine-lacks-bti`, `machine-lacks-pac`, `cpu-shows-no-fpac`, `opt-in-not-honoured`, `loader-refuses-execstack`, `link-inputs-unmatched-by-arms`, `clean-link-unmatched-by-measured`, `compile-inputs-unmatched-by-arms`, `sanitizer-group-unmeasured`, `signed-overflow-sanitized`, `lto-codegen-at-link`, `macro-contradicted-by-artifact`. A question with no referent in what was measured publishes `not-applicable`: `artifact-cannot-carry-observable`, `stdlib-lacks-observable`.

needs_vm.description: The verdict depends on the kernel: withheld under `needs-vm` where `environment.execution.mode` is `container`, and under `execution-mode-assumed` where it is `host` on an `assumed-host` basis.

premise.description: The class of `rule`'s premise in the table of the chard that wrote the report, which fixes the observation's one verdict: `toolchain-fact` publishes `unsupported`, `instrument-limitation` publishes `indeterminate`, and `inapplicable` publishes `not-applicable`. A reader sorts the observation by this class, and by its own table's only where this is absent.

reason.description: The sentence saying why `rule` withheld the check on this toolchain.

rule.description: Which rule withheld the check, so withholdings can be counted by cause without reading the sentence in `reason`. `gating` lists each rule under the verdict its premise publishes, and the `reason` of an observation a rule withheld says what tripped it.

structured_diagnostics.description: Present only under `--structured-diagnostics`, on a compiler-diag check the structured decoder has needles for: each built arm is rebuilt with the compiler's SARIF on stderr, and both decoders read the severity of the first diagnostic carrying one of the check's needles. The verdict is the prose decoder's either way, so this is evidence about the decoder, not the toolchain.

format.description: The flag the side build carried: `-fdiagnostics-format=sarif-stderr` for gcc and `-fdiagnostics-format=sarif` for clang.

arms_expected.description: How many arms the comparison was fed: 3, the measured build and both controls, the negative being the clean build where the check has no negative control. `arms` and `arms_missing` together account for every one.

arms_missing.description: Arms fed with no build of their own or no side build, so nothing was compared; each is also a warning in `diagnostics`. Absent when empty.

arms.description: Keyed by `measured`, `positive`, `negative`. An arm with no build or no side build is absent here and named in `arms_missing`.

structured.description: `note` is kept rather than folded into `warning`, where the prose decoder reads a matched line with no severity word as a warning.

reason.description: Why the side build's stream could not be decoded.

build_rejection.description: Present on `build-failed` where the toolchain refused a flag the profile supplied, so the failure is not this check's: a line on which the tool said it did not recognise something names a flag chard passed from the profile. It quotes the build's first such line, and the `profile-flag-rejected` diagnostics name each flag refused on a later one.

cwe.description: Present only where one CWE maps unambiguously; several of these mechanisms have none.

fires_at_level.description: The effective _FORTIFY_SOURCE level at which this rung begins to fire.

reference.description: A link to where a flag was argued about, for every distribution alike. A source about one distribution is a `claim`, which is filtered per report.

claim.description: What a published source claims about a flag on a distribution, carried so a measurement can be compared with it.

distro.description: os-release id, or `*` when not distribution-specific.

since.description: Release the source says it applies from; later releases are covered.

mechanism.description: Where the source says it comes from: compiler or build-system.

agrees.description: Absent when there is nothing to compare: a withheld verdict is no evidence against a claim, and a claim about another release says nothing of this one.

tables.description: ELF tables whose unread truncation concludes indeterminate under the clause @truncated.

clauses.description: Tried in order; the first whose condition holds concludes.

id.description: Unique within the predicate; never empty and never beginning with @, which the reserved clauses use.

because.description: The reason the clause concludes; it holds a character outside ECMA-262's \s.

elf_field.description: The ElfFacts keys a predicate may read, as $defs/elf_facts in chard-report.schema.json spells them.

decoded.description: One predicate reading as a value, on the measured build of every macro and `elf-static` observation that reached its decoder (`evidence.decoded`) and on every control arm with an `outcome`, whether or not the triple discriminated. A reader recomputes it by evaluating `decoders.predicates[check]` over the `facts` entries named here, the macro filter `evidence_filters.macros` where the macro map is a `macro-dump`, and the watch list `evidence_filters.symbols`, as the `decoded-reading-disagrees-with-facts` rule does.

facts.description: The `facts` key the reading's own channel was read from: the artifact digest on the `elf-static` channel; on the macro channel the artifact digest under `macro_source: compiled-artifact` or the dump's `stdout_sha256` under `preprocessor`.

macros.description: The `facts` key of the macro map an `elf-static` predicate that reads macros was evaluated over, keyed as `facts` is on the macro channel. Absent on the macro channel and on a predicate that reads no macro.

clause.description: The deciding clause's id, or one of the reserved clauses `@no-source:macros`, `@no-source:elf`, `@truncated` and `@otherwise`.

level.description: The conclusion's level, where it has one.

withholding_set.description: One of `coverage.withholding`'s two sets. Each member is counted once by verdict and once by reason: `by_verdict` sums to `count`, and `by_rule`, `by_withheld_cause` and `no_named_cause` sum to `count` between them.

by_verdict.description: The set's observations by verdict. Absent when the set is empty.

by_rule.description: The set's observations carrying a `gating.rule`, by the rule's id. Absent when none does.

by_withheld_cause.description: The set's observations with no gating rule whose control triple withheld, by `controls.withheld_because`; one carrying both is counted under its rule alone. Absent when none is counted here.

no_named_cause.description: The set's observations carrying neither a gating rule nor a triple's cause: an `indeterminate` a discriminating triple reached (its `evidence.observed` says why), or a `build-failed` or `run-failed` (its record does). Always 0 in `earned_limitations`.

digest.description: The report's verdicts and what they stand on, ahead of the evidence: the first key of every report and what `chard digest` prints, derived from the report's own fields and held to them by the `digest-disagrees-with-report` rule when `table`, `matrix` or `digest` reads the report. A report without one does not validate against this schema; `table`, `matrix` and `digest` refuse it, and `detect` replays it.

chard_schema.description: The report's `chard_schema`, so the block printed alone names its shape.

consistency.description: The report's `consistency.status`. A published report reads `consistent`; `contradicted` is found only in a report `measure` refused and kept as `<file>.contradicted`, which `chard digest` refuses.

verdict_counts.description: The observations' verdicts, counted as published, whatever the polarity: a `weaken` check's `off` (the flag's effect absent) is its protected state and is counted under `off` with the rest.

checks.description: One row per observation, in the report's order.

level.description: `observations[].level`, absent where the observation carries none.

polarity.description: `observations[].polarity`. For a `weaken` check `off` is the protected state: the flag's effect is absent.

gating.description: `observations[].gating.rule`, where a gating rule decided the verdict.

reasons.description: One entry per observation that is not a measurement (neither `on`, `off` nor `partial`), in the report's order. The sentence saying why stays in the observation: the first non-blank, in this order, of `build_rejection`, `gating.reason`, `controls.failure_reason` and `evidence.observed`. Absent when every check measured.

standing.description: Which of `coverage.withholding`'s two sets the observation is counted in: `earned-limitation` for an `unsupported` or `not-applicable` beside a `gating.rule` whose premise publishes that verdict, `instrument-withholding` for every other.

meaning.description: What a column under the profile measures against what a distribution's package build injects: one sentence per `profile.flags_source`, with a clause where `toolchain.config_files` names a file (the `driver-config-file` sentence names it already) and one where `profile.id` carries the `+env:` suffix of `--env` pairs.

harness_revision.description: `run.harness_revision`, absent where the report carries none.

harness_revision_source.description: `run.harness_revision_source`, absent where the report carries none.

harness_rustflags_sha256.description: `run.harness_rustflags_sha256`, absent where the report carries none.

withholding.description: What this report measured, what it established as a limitation, and what chard withheld: three counts adding to `checks_attempted`, with no rate, since a rate over either set reads as a grade of the toolchain, and held to the observations by the `withholding-disagrees-with-verdict-counts` rule when the report is written and when `table` or `matrix` reads it. An older block with `withheld` and no `earned_limitations` counts the two sets together and is not comparable with this one: `table` and `matrix` refuse it and name it.

published.description: Observations carrying on, off or partial.

earned_limitations.description: Observations carrying `unsupported` or `not-applicable` beside a `gating.rule` whose premise publishes that verdict: the measured system lacks the mechanism, or the question has no referent in what was measured. They settle `all_verdicts_published`.

instrument_withholdings.description: Every other observation that is not a measurement: each `probe-invalid`, `indeterminate`, `build-failed` and `run-failed`, and an `unsupported` or `not-applicable` no gating rule earns. Empty exactly when every attempted check is settled; each member is a line of a failed `--fail-on-missing`, and a check not attempted is in neither set.
